newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Printing breakdown to foil HK philately stampede.
newsitem.headline: Printing breakdown to foil HK philately stampede.

text.p: The Lunar Year of the Ox will have an inauspicious start for Hong Kong stamp dealers, whose annual rush for New Year commemoratives has been foiled after machinery that prints the stamps broke down.
The Ox Year stamps, which were to be issued this Friday, now will not appear until 20 days after the February 7 festival, the South China Morning Post said.
"It is most unfortunate that the stamps cannot be delivered on time," said an apologetic postmaster-general, Robert Footman.
Commemoratives, issued on limited print runs, always attract large crowds of dealers on the day of issue and immediately soar in value, sometimes as much as 10 times within a day or so.
Police are often deployed to deal with the stampede when tempers flare over queue-jumping.
Queues for commemoratives have swelled recently, with collector interest fuelled further by the fact that it is Hong Kong's final year under British rule.
The colony reverts to China on July 1 and Monday will be the last day that stamps bearing Queen Elizabeth's head will be sold.
